texts.li: [alpha] Wardens of {FACTION} have come to the gate with lanterns at their belts, led by {X_nameDef}. They have followed the pack that runs with {BEAST} across the region, and would like to hunt it on the colony's land, with the colony's best shot if the colony likes. They would keep its hide for their book of hunted beasts, and the meat would be the colony's.

[nemesis] {X_nameDef} and the Wardens with {X_objective} have come to the gate because {BEAST} is on the colony's land again. {X_nameDef} says the Wardens keep a page in their book for every animal that has hurt someone, and this one has never been killed. They would hunt it now, with the colony's best shot if the colony likes, for its hide. The meat would be the colony's.

[legend] Wardens of {FACTION} came to the gate as soon as they heard {BEAST} was on the colony's land. It is famous across the region, and the Wardens have been trying to hunt it for years. {X_nameDef} asks permission to hunt it here, with the colony's best shot if the colony likes, for its hide. The meat would be the colony's.

[manhunter] {X_nameDef} and the Wardens with {X_objective} have hurried up the road, because {BEAST} is loose on the colony's land and attacking people. They would go after it at once, alone or with the colony's best shot, and want nothing but its hide.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a Warden of {FACTION} with a boar-spear over one shoulder, has come to the gate with the others behind {X_objective}. {X_nameDef} says {BEAST} is on the colony's land, and the Wardens would like to hunt it, with the colony's best hunter if the colony likes, for its hide.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate with a crossbow, a book under one arm and the others behind. They track the great beasts of the region from road to road, and {BEAST} is on the colony's land. They would hunt it, with the colony's best shot if the colony likes, for its hide. The meat would be the colony's.
[their:grateful] The Wardens remember the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come to tell it that {BEAST} is on its land. They would hunt it with the colony's best shot and take only its hide.

li.label: Hunt it beside them, {A_nameDef} with them
li.outcome: The Wardens and {A_nameDef} have gone after {BEAST}. If they kill it, one of the Wardens will skin it where it lies. They keep the hide, and the meat stays with the colony.

li.label: Let them hunt it alone
li.outcome: The Wardens have gone after {BEAST} on their own. If they kill it, one of them will skin it where it lies, and the meat will be left for the colony.

li.label: Not on our land
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs, writes something in the book and leads the Wardens back to the road.

lines.li: [hunt] Keep behind the spears, and do not shoot past us.
[hunt] Its page has been open long enough.
[hunt,legend] Eleven years Garrow waited, and we will not wait that long for this one.
[hunt,nemesis] A beast that takes a person answers for it.
[fell] Into the book with you, and the page closed.
[fell] Hold its head while I start the hide.
[fell] Good meat for the colony, and a good hide for the book.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the pelt-buyer of {FACTION}'s lodge at {PLACE}, has come to the gate with a tracker and an empty pack beast, having heard the colony has hides to sell. The Wardens pay a fixed rate for good pelts, a little over their worth: {COUNT} silver for {TALE}.\n\nIf the colony likes, the tracker with {X_objective} would teach {A_nameDef} to follow a trail while they deal.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked in from the lodge at {PLACE} with a tracker to buy pelts. {X_nameDef} offers {COUNT} silver for {TALE}, a little over their worth, and the tracker would show {A_nameDef} how to follow an animal by the signs it leaves.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef}, a pelt-buyer of {FACTION}, is at the gate with a tracker and a tally book. The lodge at {PLACE} needs hides, and {X_nameDef} offers {COUNT} silver for the colony's {TALE}, the Wardens' usual rate. The tracker would spend a few hours teaching {A_nameDef} tracking, if the colony likes.

[their:grateful] The Wardens think well of the colony, and their pelt-buyer {X_nameDef} has come straight to its gate. {X_nameDef} offers {COUNT} silver for {TALE}, the Wardens' usual rate, and a tracking lesson for {A_nameDef} as a favour between friends.

li.label: Sell them the pelts ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The pelts are being carried out to {X_nameDef} at the gate, and the silver carried in.

li.label: Sell them, and have the tracker teach {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The pelts are going out to {X_nameDef}, and {B_nameDef} is walking the edges of the colony's land with {A_nameDef}, looking for tracks.

li.label: The pelts are not for sale
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods, marks the colony in the tally book, and goes back toward the road.

lines.li: [bought] Good hides, and the book will say so.
[bought] The book's rate, and every pelt counted twice.
[refused] Hides keep, and so will the offer.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a Warden of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a lantern and a red cord. The lodge at {PLACE} heard that {BEAST} killed {DEAD}. When an animal kills someone, the Wardens light a lantern at the nearest crossroads, as the first Warden did for his brother. {X_nameDef} would like to light one at the colony's gate tonight and keep watch beside it through the night, with anyone who wants to join.

[ended] {X_nameDef}, a Warden of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a lantern for {DEAD}, who was killed by {BEAST}. {X_nameDef} has heard that the animal is already dead, but the Wardens light a lantern for everyone an animal kills, and write the end of the story in their book. {X_nameDef} would light it at the colony's gate and keep watch beside it the first night.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked from the lodge at {PLACE} with a lantern for {DEAD}, who was killed by {BEAST}. {X_nameDef} says the Wardens light such a lantern at a crossroads so that everyone on the road knows someone was killed there.
[their:grateful] The Wardens think well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with a lantern for {DEAD}, who was killed by {BEAST}, to light at the gate tonight.

li.label: Light it with them, and stand its first night
li.outcome: The lantern will be lit at the gate at dusk, and those who were close to {DEAD} will keep watch beside it for the first hours with {X_nameDef}.

lines.li: Keep it lit until it is done.
Where a lantern burns, someone was taken.

li.label: Let them light it at the gate
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} will light the lantern at the gate at dusk and stand beside it through the night.

li.label: Thank them, but no lantern
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says the Wardens will still write the death in their book, and goes back to the road.

lines.li: [lit] Keep it lit until it is done.
[lit] Where a lantern burns, someone was taken.
[lit,ended] The page has its ending now, and the lantern says so.

titles.li: The Quiet Bell at the gate

texts.li: [!nobeast] Bell-keepers of {FACTION} in grey habits have come to the gate, led by {X_nameDef}, with spades and a pack animal. The raiders' bodies still lie where they fell, and {X_nameDef} says everyone deserves a funeral, even those who attacked the colony. They would bury each one beyond the wall, or carry them back to the grave-garden at {PLACE}, and say their funeral words over every one. They ask nothing for it.

[nobeast] Bell-keepers of {FACTION} in grey habits have come to the gate with spades, led by {X_nameDef}. The raiders' bodies still lie where they fell, and the bell-keepers would bury each one beyond the wall and say their funeral words over every one, as they do for friend and enemy alike. They ask nothing for it.

[theirpeople,!nobeast] Bell-keepers of {FACTION} in grey habits have come to the gate with spades and a pack animal, led by {X_nameDef}. They would see to the raiders' bodies: either a grave each beyond the wall, or the walk to the grave-garden at {PLACE}, with their funeral words said over every one. {X_nameDef} says the raiders' own people will hear that someone gave their dead a funeral, and will remember who did.

[lowtech] The bell-keepers of {FACTION}, in grey habits and with long spades, go wherever the dead lie unburied, and {X_nameDef} says the bodies near the colony have lain there long enough. They would bury them beyond the wall or carry them to the grave-garden at {PLACE}, and say their funeral words for each either way.

li.label: Graves beyond the wall, with funeral words for each
li.outcome: {X_nameDef}'s bell-keepers dug a row of graves beyond the gate, buried the raiders one to a grave, and said their funeral words over every one.

li.label: Let them carry the dead to their grave-garden
li.outcome: The bell-keepers carried the raiders to their beast one by one and led it away down the road toward {PLACE}.

li.label: We will see to them ourselves
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says the dead deserve a funeral all the same, and the bell-keepers go on their way.

lines.li: [ring] Everyone is owed a bell, even the ones who came over your wall.
[ring] Ring once for friend and foe alike.
[ring] Quiet now, you are home.
[dig] Deep enough that nothing stirs.
[dig] The ground keeps what it is given.
[load] Gently, this one has a long walk ahead.
[load] Bury them deep, and listen, that is all we do.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a bell-keeper of {FACTION} in a grey habit, has come to {DEAD}'s grave with a small bronze bell on a cord. The grave-garden at {PLACE} heard of the death, and {X_nameDef} says the bell-keepers lead the funeral of anyone whose people want it: the colony would gather at the graveside and {X_nameDef} would say the old words. If the colony would rather, {X_nameDef} could instead stand quietly at the grave for a while with one of the colonists.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a bell-keeper of {FACTION}, has walked from {PLACE} to stand at {DEAD}'s grave. The bell-keepers believe everyone who dies deserves a funeral, and {X_nameDef} would lead the colony through the funeral words if it likes.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef}, a bell-keeper of {FACTION}, is waiting quietly by {DEAD}'s grave. {X_nameDef} says the bell-keepers have led funerals in grave-gardens, on battlefields and in the back rooms of towns, and offers to lead this one, or simply to stand a while at the grave.

[their:grateful] The Quiet Bell remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} came to {DEAD}'s grave as soon as the grave-garden at {PLACE} heard of the death, to lead the funeral as if {DEAD} were one of their own.

li.label: The funeral, {X_nameDef} leading it
li.outcome: The colony is gathering at {DEAD}'s grave, and {X_nameDef} will say the funeral words when everyone is there.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} stand a while at the grave, {A_nameDef} beside {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is standing at {DEAD}'s grave with {X_nameDef}.

li.label: We will mourn our own way
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods and leaves the colony to mourn in its own way.

lines.li: [ring] Quiet now, you are home.
[ring] Everyone is owed a bell, and this one is yours.
[ring] The ground keeps what it is given, gently.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an old bell-keeper of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a bell wrapped in grey cloth. {X_nameDef} says the bell-keepers can sense what moves under the ground, and something under the colony's land has woken up. It may never come to the surface, but it would be wise to keep lights at the doors and a watch on the walls tonight. {X_nameDef} offers to stand at the gate until morning.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a bell-keeper of {FACTION}, has walked from {PLACE} with a muffled bell to warn the colony that the bell-keepers sense something awake under the ground nearby. {X_nameDef} advises a light at every door tonight and a watch on the wall, and offers to stand at the gate.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is at the gate with a bell wrapped in grey cloth, and does not want to come in. {X_nameDef} says the bell-keepers at {PLACE} watch for signs under the ground the way others watch the weather, and they have seen signs of something stirring near the colony. A watch on the walls tonight, and lamps at the doors, would be wise.

li.label: Keep a watch on the walls tonight, lamps at the doors
li.outcome: Lamps are lit at the colony's doors, and a watch will walk the walls until first light, with {X_nameDef} at the gate.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} stand at the gate with a lamp
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} has a lamp at the gate and the bell in hand, and will stand there till morning.

li.label: Thank them and send them on
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says the bell-keepers will keep watching for signs all the same, and leaves.

lines.li: [ring] Bury them deep, and listen, and tonight we listen.
[ring] I will stand here till morning and listen for you.
[thanks] Keep a light by the door, at least.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a travelling tamer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with {BEAST} and a braided violet sash covered in tokens. {X_nameDef} has heard the colony keeps animals, and challenges {A_nameDef}, its best animal handler, to a friendly bout against {BEAST}. It would be practice blows only, with nobody hurt on purpose, and the winner gets a token for the sash. {X_nameDef} says that being fairly beaten by a stranger is the greatest honour among the Circuit's tamers.

[pokemon] {X_nameDef}, a travelling tamer of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with {BEAST}, a Fighting type that is eager for a bout. {X_nameDef} challenges {A_nameDef}, the colony's best animal handler, to a fair and friendly bout against it, with a token for the winner.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked in with {BEAST} and a sash of knotted tokens, and asks for the colony's best animal handler. {X_nameDef} says the best way to judge someone with animals is a friendly bout, and challenges {A_nameDef} to face {BEAST} with practice blows, a token going to the winner.
[their:grateful] The Circuit thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has gone out of {X_possessive} way to challenge {A_nameDef} to a friendly bout against {BEAST}, as old rivals do.

li.label: {A_nameDef} takes the challenge
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is stepping up to {BEAST} for a friendly bout, with {X_nameDef} calling the blows.

li.label: Have {X_objective} show {A_nameDef} what {BEAST} can do instead
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is sitting with {X_nameDef} while {BEAST} shows off everything it knows.

li.label: Not today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} laughs, says the challenge stands, and goes on with {BEAST}.

lines.li: [challenge] A bond is not a leash, so show me yours.
[challenge] Fair blows only, and may the better keeper win.
[won] To be beaten fairly is an honour, and here is your token.
[won] You beat us fairly, and the Circuit will hear your name.
[lost] A good bout, and you will win the next one.
[lost] Win their trust and they will win your battles, you are nearly there.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an egg-trader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a basket kept warm in straw. It holds {TALE} from the Circuit's hatchery at {PLACE}, a kind the colony doesn't keep. {X_nameDef} would swap them for one of the colony's own fertile eggs, or sell them for {COUNT} silver.

[!ours] {X_nameDef}, an egg-trader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with {TALE} in a straw-lined basket, from the hatchery at {PLACE}. The colony has no fertile eggs to swap, but {X_nameDef} would sell them for {COUNT} silver.

[pokemon] {X_nameDef}, an egg-trader of {FACTION}, has brought {TALE} from the Circuit's hatchery, kept warm in a padded box that hums faintly. {X_nameDef} would swap them for one of the colony's own fertile eggs or sell them for {COUNT} silver, and whatever hatches will be the colony's to raise.

[their:grateful] The Circuit thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has brought {TALE} from the hatchery at {PLACE}. As a friend, {X_nameDef} would swap them for one of the colony's eggs or sell them for {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Swap one of our fertile eggs for them
li.outcome: One of the colony's eggs is being carried out to {X_nameDef}, and the Circuit's are set down at the gate, warm in their straw.

li.label: Buy them ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, and the eggs are set down at the gate in their straw.

li.label: No eggs today
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} tucks the straw back round the eggs and goes on.

lines.li: [egg] Keep them warm, and talk to them, they hear you.
[egg] Every egg is a road not walked yet.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a ranger of {FACTION}, has walked up to the gate with {BEAST} on a lead. The Circuit's rangers know the animals along the region's roads, and {X_nameDef} says this one belongs to the colony: it strayed and has been living wild. {A_nameDef} would know it anywhere.

[wild] {X_nameDef}, a ranger of {FACTION}, has come to the gate leading {BEAST}, which went wild and left the colony months ago. It took {X_nameDef} a week to win its trust again, and {X_nameDef} thinks it would like to come home. {A_nameDef} would know it anywhere.
[their:grateful] The Circuit thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef}, one of its rangers, has brought {BEAST} home, found wandering far from the colony's land.

li.label: Take {BEAST} home, with thanks
li.outcome: {BEAST} is the colony's again, at the gate where {X_nameDef} handed over the lead.

li.label: Take {BEAST} home, and give {X_nameDef} something for the trouble ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: {BEAST} is the colony's again, and the silver for {X_nameDef}'s trouble is being carried out to the gate.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} keep {BEAST}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} scratches {BEAST} behind the ears and leads it away with the Circuit.

lines.li: [home] Home again, and no leash needed.
[home] It knew the way, it only needed company.
[keep] A bond is not a leash, and it chose to follow me.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a fixer of {FACTION}, has pulled up at the gate on a cart hung with tools, wearing a much-patched coat with a brass cog stitched to the shoulder. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} offers to mend every worn coat and damaged weapon in the colony by morning, before the Wheel moves on tomorrow.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has drawn a cart up to the gate, its sides hung with awls, files and pots of glue, and offers to mend everything the colony wears or fights with for {COUNT} silver before the Wheel moves on.

[industrial|spacer] {X_nameDef}, a fixer of {FACTION}, has a portable grinder and a welding mask on the cart, and offers to mend every worn coat and battered weapon in the colony for {COUNT} silver before the Wheel's yard moves on.
[their:grateful] The Wheel thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} offers a friend's price: {COUNT} silver to mend every piece, with a lesson thrown in if anyone wants one.

li.label: Pay {COUNT} silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} worked through the pile one piece at a time and mended every piece, closing seams, riveting straps and sharpening edges.

li.label: No, thank you
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs, says the Wheel will be back round, and drives on.

li.label: Pay a little to have {X_objective} teach {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} spent the evening showing {A_nameDef} how the Wheel mends things, such as patching a coat so that the patch lasts longer than the coat, and left the mending itself to {A_objective}.

lines.li: [mend] Nothing is broken, only waiting.
[mend] Mend it tonight, we leave tomorrow.
[refused] The Wheel comes round again, it always does.

texts.li: Scrap-runners of {FACTION} have come to the gate with an empty cart, and {X_nameDef} is doing the talking. {X_nameDef} says the Wheel buys what others throw away, and the colony has {TALE} lying about. They would pay {COUNT} silver for all of it, or trade a {THING} that the Wheel has repaired to as good as new.
[nopiece] Scrap-runners of {FACTION} have come to the gate with an empty cart, {X_nameDef} doing the talking. The colony has {TALE} lying about, and the Wheel would give {COUNT} silver for the lot.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} and the scrap-runners of {FACTION} have pushed a handcart up to the gate and want to buy {TALE}, since the Wheel melts down, mends and resells everything. They offer {COUNT} silver for the lot, or a {THING} of theirs, repaired to as good as new.
[their:grateful] The Wheel thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef}'s runners have come straight to it to buy {TALE}. As friends, they offer {COUNT} silver, or a {THING} repaired to as good as new.

li.label: Sell them the scrap ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The scrap is being carried out to {X_nameDef}'s cart at the gate, and the silver carried in.

li.label: Trade it for the mended {THING}
li.outcome: The scrap is going out to the cart, and {X_nameDef} is setting the mended {THING} down at the gate.

li.label: Keep the scrap
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} says the colony will change its mind when the heap gets bigger, and the runners push the cart back to the road.

lines.li: [scrap] Buy it cheap, sell it better.
[scrap] If it rolls, it comes with us, and this rolls well enough.
[refused] Heaps only get bigger, we will be back.

texts.li: Runners of {FACTION} have hurried up the road, led by {X_nameDef}. The Wheel heard there is a wrecked {BEAST} {PLACE}, and a wrecked mechanoid is the best scrap there is. They would strip it where it lies and give half the parts to the colony, or buy it whole for {COUNT} silver and take everything.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef} and the runners of {FACTION} hurried over when they heard of the wrecked machine {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} says the Wheel knows how to take one apart, and offers either to split the metal and parts half and half with the colony, or to pay {COUNT} silver for all of it.

[their:grateful] The Wheel thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef}'s runners came as soon as they heard of the wrecked {BEAST} {PLACE}. They would strip it where it lies and give half to the colony, or pay {COUNT} silver for the lot.

li.label: Let them strip it, half for us
li.outcome: The runners are at the wreck with their tools, and half of what they take off it will be left there for the colony.

li.label: Sell it to them whole ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is coming in from the gate, and the runners are taking the wreck apart for themselves.

li.label: The wreck is ours
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} looks at the wreck a long moment, says it is a waste, and the runners go.

lines.li: [strip] Nothing is broken, only waiting, and this one waited long enough.
[strip] Mind the core, it bites even dead.
[refused] That is a whole season of parts, but it is yours.
